ana: Thanks again for the all-hands — quick follow-up on infra capacity. What's the plan for burst GPU pools over the upcoming holiday window? Are we sticking to preemptible-only for burst or buying short-term reserved capacity?

jamal: Short answer: burst will be primarily preemptible where acceptable, with targeted reserved top-ups for critical enterprise tiers. We want to avoid heavy spend on short windows.

lucy: timeline for the reserved top-ups?

jamal: Pilot for the new burst orchestration next Tue (canary opens 10:00 PST). If pilot looks good we scale the reserved top-ups by region over the next 2–3 weeks. Full holiday config aimed to be live before the end-of-quarter traffic test.

simon: How will autoscaler behave during a sudden spike if preemptibles drop out? Any graceful fallback?

jamal: autoscaler policy has a fallback matrix: 1) try preemptible pool, 2) if preemptible capacity < threshold for 90s then route to reserved pool (if customer tier allows), 3) if reserved not available then route to smaller model variants (latency might go up). Canary uses traffic-weighted routing (10% canary -> 100% if stable).

katie: Can you share the canary and autoscaler knobs? Ops needs to prep runbooks.

jamal: pasted quick excerpt from the canary policy below:

```
# canary routing snippet
canary_fraction: 0.10
canary_duration: 30m
fallback_policy:
  preemptible_threshold_secs: 90
  reserved_fallback: true
  model_variant_fallback: true
autoscaler_metrics:
  - queue_depth
  - gpu_utilization
  - median_latency
scale_up_cooldown: 20s
scale_down_cooldown: 2m
```

ana (typo): devs will we need any config changes in client SDKs?

ana: (meant to type lucy)

lucy: I can update SDK flags if there are any required; prefer server-side routing to avoid churn.

jamal: No client changes for basic routing. If customers want to opt into reserved-fallback or set strict latency SLOs we will expose a per-customer flag (server-side) — will surface in console.

ana: APAC question: is regional supply still the blocker for H100/80GB spots?

jamal: APAC is tighter. Procurement ETA for additional H100 racks slipped ~3 weeks (vendor backlog). For APAC holiday spikes we'll rely more on regional capacity shaping + cross-region routing to eu-west/us-west for non-sensitive traffic. Private deployments unaffected.

devops-bot: deploy_status: burst-orch-v2 scheduled for canary at 2028-05-14T17:00:00Z by jamal.

katie: Ops action items: 1) update runbook for fallback routing, 2) prepare communication for enterprise customers about reserved top-ups, 3) monitor canary and report at +30m. I'll create tickets after this thread.

ana: thanks all — appreciate the clarity. Will loop in customer success for higher-tier accounts who asked about guaranteed holiday capacity. :thumbsup:

simon: one quick ask — can we add a small synthetic test that simulates preemptible losses so we can validate fallback logic during canary?

jamal: good idea. i'll add a synthetic scenario to the canary job (failure mode: 50% preemptible kill after 60s).

lucy: cheers, see notes in infra channel when available.

katie: created ticket INFRA-4821 with the runbook updates and synthetic test checklist.

ana: perfect — closing the loop here.
